RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Rowan Brooks
Member ID: W579327479
Reference Number: POC-D47F9A88CC-69885
Date of Notice: 2026-08-23
Requested Service/Procedure: Shoulder labral / instability repair, CPT 29806
Treating Surgeon: Marchetti, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Appeals Review Committee:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 29806 (arthroscopic shoulder capsulorrhaphy/labral repair), as stated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-23. The stated reason for denial was that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I respectfully disagree and ask that the plan reconsider this determination in light of the clinical record summarized below.

Basis for this appeal

My understanding is that Anthem applies the Carelon Medical Benefits Management "Joint Surgery" Clinical Appropriateness Guideline (Musculoskeletal Appropriate Use Criteria, Doc ID MSK02-1125.1, Effective Date 11/15/2025) to requests for shoulder arthroscopy procedures such as CPT 29806. That guideline states, in the Shoulder Arthroscopy and Open Procedures section:

"Capsulorrhaphy is considered medically necessary when ALL the following criteria are met: History of a shoulder dislocation or recurrent subluxation ... Shoulder pain and/or instability which interferes with age-appropriate activities of daily living [ADLs] ... Physical exam consistent with symptomatic glenohumeral instability (e.g., apprehension, relocation, sulcus sign, load and shift)."

The same guideline also sets out this general framework for any requested intervention:

"Prior to any intervention, it is essential that the clinician confirms the diagnosis or establishes its pretest likelihood based on a complete evaluation of the patient. This includes a history and physical examination and, where applicable, a review of relevant laboratory studies, diagnostic testing, and response to prior therapeutic intervention."

I was not able to obtain the complete text of every bullet in the guideline's Capsulorrhaphy criteria (including any additional, separately worded imaging-specific requirement that may exist in the full document), and I am not quoting or attributing any language to the plan beyond what is shown above. If the denial rests on additional criteria not quoted here, I request that Anthem identify the specific criterion or criteria that were found unmet, with the exact policy language, so that the record can be directly addressed.

Application of the clinical record to the stated criteria

1. History of a shoulder dislocation or recurrent subluxation: Mr. Brooks has experienced three anterior shoulder dislocations since symptom onset approximately 12 months ago, the most recent of which required reduction in the emergency department. This is a documented history of recurrent dislocation, not merely subluxation.

2. Shoulder pain and/or instability which interferes with age-appropriate activities of daily living: The record documents that Mr. Brooks avoids overhead reaching and cannot return to work involving lifting due to instability. This represents a direct functional limitation on daily and occupational activities caused by the shoulder condition.

3. Physical exam consistent with symptomatic glenohumeral instability: The surgeon's examination documented positive apprehension and relocation tests and increased anterior translation on load-and-shift testing — the specific examination findings referenced in the guideline — with full strength and no signs of infection.

4. Imaging: An MR arthrogram of the shoulder performed 2026-07-29 demonstrated an anteroinferior labral tear (Bankart lesion) with a small Hill-Sachs lesion, glenoid bone loss under 10%, and an intact rotator cuff. This is the anatomic correlate of the recurrent-dislocation history and the positive instability examination findings, and it directly supports — rather than contradicts — the clinical diagnosis of anterior glenohumeral instability with a Bankart lesion for which arthroscopic capsulorrhaphy/labral repair (CPT 29806) is the standard operative treatment.

5. Failed conservative management: Mr. Brooks completed 10 weeks (20 visits) of supervised physical therapy focused on rotator cuff and scapular stabilizer strengthening with activity modification (2026-04-16 through 2026-06-25), as documented in the physical therapy discharge note, in addition to six months of NSAID use during symptomatic flares. Injection therapy was not pursued because it is not indicated for instability. Despite this structured course of conservative care, Mr. Brooks continued to have recurrent dislocation events, confirming failure of non-operative management.

6. No contraindications: The record documents no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and non-smoker status, none of which raise any of the safety concerns addressed elsewhere in the guideline's general framework.

Taken together, the history of recurrent dislocation, the functional impact on daily activities and work, the positive instability examination findings, the corroborating MR arthrogram findings of a Bankart lesion, and the documented failure of a structured course of conservative management collectively support that CPT 29806 is medically necessary for this patient under the criteria quoted above.

Requested action

I ask that Anthem/Carelon reverse the denial and approve CPT 29806 as requested by Dr. Marchetti. If the denial is upheld, I request:

- A copy of the complete medical necessity criteria actually applied to this request, including any imaging-specific criterion not addressed above;
- A peer-to-peer review between Dr. Marchetti and the plan's reviewing physician; and
- Written confirmation of my right to a subsequent level of internal appeal and to external review, including instructions on how and where to file each.

Enclosed with this appeal

- Physical therapy discharge note documenting 20 visits of supervised PT, 2026-04-16 to 2026-06-25
- MR arthrogram report dated 2026-07-29
- Office visit/exam notes documenting apprehension, relocation, and load-and-shift testing
- Emergency department record of reduced anterior dislocation
- Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Marchetti
- Copy of the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-23 (Reference No. POC-D47F9A88CC-69885)

This appeal is being submitted within the 180-day appeal window stated in the denial notice, which expires 2027-02-19.

Please direct all correspondence regarding this appeal to me at the address, phone number, and email listed above, and to Dr. Marchetti's office at [surgeon's office phone/fax] for any clinical follow-up.

Sincerely,

Rowan Brooks
Member ID: W579327479
